title: Recall Quiz: Modern Age II: Yeats, Shaw, Beckett

questions.q: The famous lines 'Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold' appear in which prophetic poem by W.B. Yeats?
questions.explanation: This poem envisions the breakdown of society after WWI.

questions.q: George Bernard Shaw revolutionized the English stage by creating which type of play, focused on intellectual debate and social critique?
questions.explanation: Shaw despised melodrama and used the stage as a platform for debate.

questions.q: In Shaw's 'Pygmalion', Professor Henry Higgins wagers that he can pass off a flower girl as a duchess simply by doing what?
questions.explanation: The play is a satire on how the British class system judges people primarily on their accents.

questions.q: Samuel Beckett's 'Waiting for Godot' is the defining masterpiece of which post-WWII theatrical movement?
questions.explanation: Absurdist theatre strips away traditional plot to reflect the existential meaninglessness of life.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the plot of 'Waiting for Godot'?
options: Two tramps waiting endlessly on a barren road for a man who never arrives
A complex murder mystery solved by a detective
A family dispute over a large inheritance
questions.explanation: It is famously known as a play where 'nothing happens, twice'.

questions.q: Which poem by Yeats deals with the theme of aging and the desire to escape the physical body into the eternal world of art?
questions.explanation: Byzantium represents an eternal, artificial world of perfect art.

questions.q: Shaw's play 'Arms and the Man' is primarily a satire targeting:
options: The romanticized, glorious view of war and soldiers
questions.explanation: It contrasts the romantic ideals of war with the unheroic reality of actual soldiers.

questions.q: Which of these three Irish writers was a central figure in the 'Irish Literary Revival' and a founder of the Abbey Theatre?
questions.explanation: Yeats was deeply committed to reviving Irish mythology and cultural identity.
